newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end down, undertone remains firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end down, undertone remains firm.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Tuesday as earlier gains turned into losses on declines by U.S. Treasuries, although traders reported the undertone remains solid.
"The market is still very strong. We continued to follow the U.S.," said a trader at a local bank. Activity was slim, players said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/8 at 93-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was down $0.30 at 117.40.
Another trader said there were slim flows this session with "mostly local banks trading in and out," of the market.
Players say the firm tone from last week when spreads fell to record lows remains intact but further gains will depend on the performance of U.S. Treasuries and the course of U.S. monetary policy.
U.S. retail sale producer price figures due to be released later in the week will be watched closely.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 5.53 percent.
